inputs.original_text: This looks less like a paperwork mistake and more like a deliberate setup: people went to immigration court seeking legal status, and ICE lawyers used a memo as cover to arrest and detain thousands—even though prosecutors now say the memo didn’t authorize those arrests. The admission only came out in newly filed court documents, which raises the question of how long officials expected that justification to hold. The system appears to have turned court attendance into a trap, then relied on legal language to make it look legitimate.
inputs.modified_text: This wasn’t just a paperwork error. People showed up in immigration court seeking legal status, and ICE lawyers used a memo to justify arresting and detaining thousands—now prosecutors say it didn’t even authorize those arrests. That reversal looks less like accountability than a controlled retreat: the system used legal language to turn court attendance into a trap, then backed away from the memo once it became harder to defend. The real question is who decided this was acceptable, and how long they thought the cover story would work.
